questions.q: What problem do Named Credentials solve?
options: Session timeout configuration
MFA enrollment for internal users
Inbound SSO for users logging into Salesforce
Outbound authentication, letting Apex/Flow callouts authenticate to external systems without hardcoding credentials
questions.explain: Named Credentials manage outbound authentication from Salesforce to external systems, bundling the endpoint and auth configuration so credentials never appear directly in Apex code.

questions.q: When should a Named Credential use the Per-User identity type instead of Named Principal?
options: When the external system needs to enforce its own user-specific authorization, such as showing each user only their own data
Never; Per-User is deprecated
Only for integrations that don't require any authentication at all
Always, regardless of the integration's purpose
questions.explain: Per-User authenticates each Salesforce user individually with the external system, which is necessary when the external system needs genuine per-user accountability or authorization, unlike Named Principal's single shared identity.

questions.q: What happens if Named Principal is used for an integration that actually needed per-user accountability on the external system?
options: The external system automatically switches to Per-User mode
Nothing changes; the two identity types behave identically
Everyone's activity collapses into one shared identity, defeating any downstream accountability the external system might otherwise enforce
The integration automatically fails to authenticate
questions.explain: Named Principal uses one fixed identity for all outbound calls — using it where individual accountability is needed silently erases the distinction between which Salesforce user actually triggered each call.

questions.q: In the current (non-Legacy) Named Credential schema, what does the External Credential object hold?
options: The user's Salesforce profile assignment
The org's Session Settings
Only the endpoint URL
The actual authentication protocol (e.g., OAuth 2.0, JWT Bearer) and the Named Principal/Per-User identity type
questions.explain: The current schema splits the Named Credential (endpoint/callout options) from the External Credential (the actual auth protocol and identity type), allowing reuse of one External Credential across multiple Named Credentials.

questions.q: Why is the lesson's framing of Named Credentials as 'the mirror image of the rest of the course' accurate?
options: Because the same protocols covered for inbound authentication (OAuth, JWT Bearer, certificate trust) reappear here, just facing outward from Salesforce instead of inward
Because Named Credentials replace the need for Connected Apps entirely
Because Named Credentials only apply to SAML, never OAuth
Because Named Credentials have nothing to do with OAuth, JWT, or certificates
questions.explain: The same authentication protocols studied for inbound SSO and provisioning reappear in Named Credentials/External Credentials, just used for Salesforce authenticating outbound to other systems rather than other systems authenticating into Salesforce.
